issue_asks: `#d {id}` with toc + attr_list must not raise TypeError
Crash must be fixed with and without a [TOC] marker
A valueless id should behave as if no id was given (normal slug generated)
Headings with a real id like `# Title {#my-id}` must keep working unchanged

findings.problem: `not el.attrib.get("id")` also treats an explicit empty id (`{id=""}`) as missing, so a slug is now generated where before the empty id was kept. This is arguably better (an empty id is invalid HTML), but it is a small behaviour change beyond the issue. Also line 392 still adds the None value to `used_ids`; this is harmless.

reviewer.summary: The one-line fix in toc.py treats a None id as missing, so a slug is generated. I ran the full suite (all pass) and my own probes. `#d {id}` renders `<h1 id="d">`. Duplicate bare ids get unique slugs (a, a_1). A bare id next to a real id `{#a}` gets a_1 and does not clash. The TOC, anchorlink and permalink outputs are all correct. Explicit ids are untouched. The two new tests check the issue's exact input, with and without [TOC], and no existing tests were changed. The only side effect is that an empty `id=""` now also gets a slug, which is a minor point.

decision.why: every checklist item is true and there is no blocker/major finding
